disease_label_per_paper: Serotonin syndrome precipitated by cocaine and fentanyl in a patient taking oxycodone/paracetamol, trazodone, and mirtazapine
presentation_summary: 37-year-old woman with bipolar disorder was found confused on the floor after applying a friend's fentanyl patch before sleep.
She was prescribed oxycodone/paracetamol, trazodone, and mirtazapine, and urine drug screen was positive for cocaine metabolites, opiates, cannabinoids, and benzodiazepine.
She had a witnessed seizure with urine incontinence before hospital arrival and another seizure after naloxone.
Emergency department vitals showed BP 165/81 mmHg, HR 184/min, RR 39/min, and temperature 104 F.
Exam showed extreme agitation, dilated nonreactive pupils, total body rigidity, ocular clonus, inducible and spontaneous lower-extremity myoclonus, and grade 4 hyperreflexia.
Labs showed WBC 14000/mcL, sodium 132 mEq/L, bicarbonate 16 mmol/L, and lactate 5.5 mmol/L.
She received lorazepam, was intubated for GCS 6, sedated with propofol, actively cooled, given cyproheptadine via NG tube, extubated the next day, and discharged after improvement.
